Third, a layer-fusion and FFN-partition dataflow minimizes off-chip traffic for intermediate activations and reduces the on-chip memory requirement. Implemented for the action expert of the $\pi _{0}$ VLA model, the proposed design achieves 903.2 GOPS and 111.09 GOPS/W. In asynchronous action planning, it sustains a control rate of 77.48 Hz with an energy efficiency of 85 mJ/token, and is validated in both simulation and real-robot deployment on an SO-101 platform. These results demonstrate that the proposed accelerator enables real-time and energy-efficient edge-side deployment of VLA action planning for embodied robotic control.

item.title: An RF Energy Harvesting System Supporting a 15-dB Input Power Range Using Digital Gate-Bias Relocation and Dynamic Voltage Scaling
item.description: This paper proposes an RF energy harvesting system capable of operating over a wide input power range. The system incorporates a reconfigurable rectifier with a proposed digital gate-bias relocation technique to enhance power conversion efficiency under high input power conditions. The rectifier configuration and gate-bias tuning are jointly managed by a dual-parameter maximum power point tracking (DMPPT) controller, enabling efficient operation across a broad input range. Furthermore, the rectifier output feeds a load-modulation and dynamic voltage-regulation unit that functions as a variable load, adjusting the system output voltage in response to input power variations and thereby facilitating MPPT. A tunable matching network is also employed to maintain proper impedance matching under both high- and low-power scenarios. In addition, a pipeline startup scheme is introduced to accelerate the system startup time. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RF energy harvesting system achieves a 15-dB high efficiency input power range and a peak efficiency of 32.5% at 0 dBm.

item.title: A DVS-Enabled SIMO Converter Using Adaptive Dual-Window Synthetic Current Control for 0.02 mV/mA Cross Regulation and 90.8% Peak Efficiency
item.description: This paper presents a single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) converter employing an adaptive dual-window synthetic current (ADSC) control scheme to achieve fast dynamic voltage scaling (DVS) and low cross-regulation. The proposed ADSC architecture establishes the fundamental control boundary by stacking multiple error-amplifier outputs to generate an adaptive lower hysteresis boundary, thereby enabling inherent multi-output coordination and stable regulation. To further improve transient performance, an adaptive window scaling (AWS) technique dynamically adjusts the upper hysteresis boundary according to load conditions, achieving a load-transient sensitivity of 0.103 mV/mA while reducing cross-regulation sensitivity to 0.02 mV/mA. For rapid voltage transitions, a pre-request DVS control (PDC) loop directly updates the control boundary upon receiving the voltage identification (VID) command, enabling tracking rates of 227 mV/ $\mu $ s and 50 mV/ $\mu $ s during voltage up- and down-transitions, respectively. In addition, a frequency-locked gain control amplifier (FL-GCA) provides unified control across different conduction modes by maintaining a fixed switching frequency in both continuous-conduction mode (CCM) and light-load discontinuous-conduction mode (DCM), while activating a PFM-like frequency-reduction mechanism only under ultra-light-load conditions. Fabricated in a 0.18- $\mu $ m CMOS process, the prototype achieves a peak efficiency of 90.8%.

item.title: A 28-nm 64-kb Bit-Rotated Hybrid Domain Computing-in-Memory Macro for High-Performance Computing
item.description: The development of computing-in-memory (CIM) has gone through the era of analog domain CIM, which pursued extreme energy efficiency and area efficiency, and the era of digital domain CIM, which pursued extreme computational precision. Currently, research is exploring hybrid domain CIM designs that combine the advantages of both analog and digital approaches. In order to find a better balance point between computational precision and hardware efficiency, this work proposes a bit-rotated hybrid domain CIM design which primarily employs: 1) a bit-rotated feature-in hybrid structure to achieve the optimal boundary segmentation (better computational precision) with lower hardware overhead; 2) an embedded sign-bit-processing SRAM array, enabling sign-bit extension with low hardware overhead; 3) an multi-bit-fusion scheme for low-power multi-bit quantization; and 4) a dual-granularity cooperative quantizer based on the charge domain, supporting low-power multi-cycle quantization. A 64 kb bit-rotated hybrid-domain CIM chip was fabricated with TSMC 28 nm. It supports efficient hybrid multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations and achieves 21.04–67.8 TOPS/W in energy efficiency and 0.41–1.57 TOPS/mm2 in area efficiency, which can be used to accelerate various CNN and Transformer based inference tasks.

item.title: BAPE: A Binary or Ternary-Weights Transformer Accelerator Based on Precomputation at the Edge
item.description: Binary and ternary weights substantially reduce model storage and weight-memory traffic in large language models. However, conventional GEMM independently reduces each output column, repeatedly generating candidate partial dot products for the same activation row and thus underusing ultra-low-bit computation. We present BAPE, a precomputation-based FPGA accelerator core for binary- and ternary-weight Transformer linear layers. BAPE schedules and retains candidates by complete activation row. Each activation group’s candidate partial dot products are generated once, indexed and reused across output columns by streamed weight patterns, and accumulated across groups on chip. The Precomputation Unit (PCU) and dual-mode Adder Tree Processing Engine (ATPE) reuse the same hierarchical adder tree for candidate generation and lookup-based accumulation. Joint exploration of precomputation granularity $\alpha $ and resource-sharing parallelism $\beta $ balances candidate-space size, parallel utilization, routing, timing, and power. Implemented on a Xilinx ZCU102 FPGA, BAPE supports W1.58A8/W1.58A4 BitNet-b1.58-2B-4T and W1A8/W1A4 Bonsai-4B. At the 300-MHz target, it achieves 614.40–2457.60 equivalent GOPS and 9.31–37.23 GOPS/kLUT. During model-level on-board inference with these four configurations, the measured dynamic power is 5.443–6.478 W, corresponding to a projected energy efficiency of 112.88–426.52 GOPS/W. Relative to same-precision GPU quantized inference, the maximum ACC loss is 0.351 percentage points, and the absolute per-dataset PPL change across the 24 paired results is at most 0.11%. These results show that BAPE efficiently executes low-bit linear computation for binary- and ternary-weight Transformers while preserving model inference quality.

item.title: A 19.8-Gb/s/Wire Single-Ended PAM-3/NRZ Simultaneous Bidirectional Transceiver With Shared ZQ/Hybrid Calibration for Memory Interfaces
item.description: This paper presents a single-ended simultaneous bidirectional (SBD) transceiver for pin-limited memory interfaces and demonstrates dual-mode NRZ/PAM-3 operation. To increase aggregate throughput without pushing the Nyquist frequency, the proposed architecture combines a low-V ${}_{DDQ}$ voltage-mode transmitter (TX) with a voltage-current/resistance (V-IR) hybrid that suppresses the locally transmitted outbound signal at the receiver (RX). A shared calibration scheme reuses the conventional ZQ pin to calibrate both TX impedance and hybrid current, improving robustness to process variation without additional calibration pins. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, the prototype operates over a wire-bonded off-chip channel and achieves 16 Gb/s/wire (8 Gb/s per direction) in NRZ mode at V ${}_{\textit {DDQ}}$ /V ${}_{\textit {DD}}=0.6$ /1.0 V, and 19.8 Gb/s/wire (9.9 Gb/s per direction) in PAM-3 mode at 0.8/1.2 V, with BER below $10^{-12}$ . The measured return loss is lower than -13.5 dB up to the Nyquist frequency. The measured energy efficiencies are 1.19 pJ/bit (NRZ) and 1.33 pJ/bit (PAM-3), demonstrating that multi-level single-ended SBD signaling can serve as a complementary bandwidth-scaling option for future memory interfaces.

item.title: An Energy-Efficient Hybrid Circuit Design Using Double-Tail Strong-Arm Latch for Full Duplex Communication
item.description: The continuous demand for high-speed data transfer has driven significant interest in full duplex (FD) communication, where transmission and reception occur simultaneously over the same channel. However, this concurrent operation leads to the superposition of the signal on the interconnect, making accurate extraction of the desired signal at the receiver is challenging. To successfully recover the desired signal at the receiver end from this overlapped signal, a hybrid circuit is essential. Therefore, this work introduces a hybrid circuit using a Double-Tail Strong-ARM Latch (DTSAL) for the first time. The DTSAL extracts the received signal and produces a full-swing output signal within the same circuit. The proposed hybrid circuit topology offers several advantages, including zero static power consumption and a rail-to-rail output, without requiring additional complex circuits. This approach reduces the circuit complexity while enhancing energy efficiency. A prototype has been developed using a 65 nm CMOS process with a 1.2 V supply over a 20 cm FR4 channel. The measured power of the proposed hybrid topology is only 6.94 mW, with an energy efficiency of 0.57 pJ/bit. It has been observed that the measured eye height is 444 mV at 12 Gb/s FD data rates.

item.title: A Robust Self-Calibrated Dual-RON Paths Gate Driver With Tri-Level Gate Control for Optimized Turn-On of GaN Gate Injection Transistors
item.description: This paper proposes a GaN-based gate driver optimized for gate injection transistors (GITs), whose current-driven gate behavior renders conventional voltage-driven drivers inefficient. A self-calibrated dual-RON-path architecture is introduced to meet the unique drive requirements by delivering both high transient turn-on current and low-loss steady-state current. In addition, a tri-level gate-control scheme is employed to handle hard-switching conditions, improving coupling immunity and suppressing third-quadrant conduction in half-bridge operation. Fabricated in a 0.5- $\mu $ m GaN process, the proposed driver achieves a peak output current of 1.93 A and supports up to 1200 W in a 400-V boost converter. Experimental results demonstrate up to $2\times $ reduction in driver power loss compared to conventional RC-interface and Schottky-gate drivers. The converter achieves a peak efficiency of 97.62%, while the conduction-loss increase from $50~^{\circ }$ C to $100~^{\circ }$ C is limited to $1.27\times $ , indicating enhanced thermal robustness and reduced power loss.

item.title: A 3-MHz All-NMOS Adaptive Active Gate Driver With Dual-Buffer Architecture and Detection-Free CSIV Spike Suppression for SiC MOSFETs
item.description: This paper presents the on-chip all-NMOS adaptive active gate driver (ANA-AGD) for high-speed, high-voltage SiC MOSFET applications. A dual-floating dual-buffer architecture enables inherent suppression of Common Source Inductance Voltage (CSIV)-induced oscillations without auxiliary sensing circuits. By forming two floating source-buffer paths with distinct frequency responses, the architecture generates a transient voltage difference in response to high-frequency CSIV components, enabling implicit spike discrimination without explicit sensing circuits. An active float bridge (AFB) is introduced to ensure reliable signal transmission across floating domains, preventing signal distortion and device overstress under high-voltage operation. In addition, an adaptive drive strength (ADS) structure dynamically regulates the gate-driving current through a frequency-dependent mechanism, limiting excessive current during fast transients while enhancing drive capability during the Miller plateau region. The proposed driver is fabricated using TSMC $0.18~\mu $ m CMOS HV BCD (T18HVG2) process. Measurements validate operation from 1 kHz to 3 MHz while driving a 1.2-kV SiC MOSFET. The proposed driver achieves a rise time below 25 ns at 500 kHz and an average power consumption of 58 mW. Compared to a widely-used commercial gate driver, the overshoot rate is significantly reduced from 47.3% to 1.4%, confirming effective suppression of CSIV-induced oscillations. These results demonstrate that the proposed ANA-AGD provides a compact, power-efficient, and high-speed solution for robust SiC MOSFET gate driving without requiring explicit sensing circuitry.

item.title: A High Cross-Domain Accuracy and Energy-Efficient sEMG-Based Hand Gesture Recognition Processor Supporting Hybrid-Label Online Learning Based on CDEM
item.description: Surface electromyographic (sEMG)-based hand gesture recognition (HGR) is a promising technique for AI glasses and VR devices control. However, its practical deployment is mainly restricted by recognition accuracy degradation caused by sEMG signal variability across individuals and time. Although a few sEMG HGR processors have proposed online learning to address the issue, they either achieve insufficient accuracy improvement or introduce significant energy overhead, making them difficult to be implemented on edge devices. In this work, a hand gesture recognition processor is proposed based on a state-of-the-art cross-domain error minimization (CDEM) learning method. The processor solves the problem with three key features: 1) a hybrid-label CDEM (HL-CDEM) online learning architecture to enable low-energy continuous CDEM learning in non-cross-day scenarios; 2) an inference-learning integrated reconfigurable (ILIR) architecture to decrease hardware resources for recognition model inference and online learning; 3) a composite-confidence-driven adaptive two-stage feature extraction (CCFE) architecture to decrease CNN inference energy consumption. Implemented and evaluated on the Artix-7 FPGA board, the processor achieves the energy consumption per recognition of $4.16\mu $ J, and SOTA inter-subject accuracy of 83.90% on the Ninapro DB1 dataset. Implemented with 40nm CMOS technology, the processor achieves a lower energy consumption of 49.75 nJ per recognition, lower than those of SOTA cross-domain recognition processors.

item.title: SHARP: An Energy-Efficient Spike-Based 3-D Recognition Processor With Hierarchical Hybrid Sparsity Awareness on Point Cloud
item.description: LiDAR-based 3D recognition leverages exceptional spatial granularity and broad sensory coverage to achieve high-precision perception in complex outdoor environments. Despite these advantages, the prohibitive computational workload makes real-time deployment on resource-limited edge devices a significant challenge. High-fidelity point cloud processing typically demands deep network structure, thus requiring massive operations and consuming many resource-intensive multipliers in conventional DNN accelerators. Moreover, conventional data representations and computing architectures become suboptimal under the dynamic sparsity among partitioned data tiles. In this paper, we propose SHARP, a novel spiking reconfigurable accelerator featuring hierarchical hybrid sparsity awareness on 3D point cloud based recognition tasks. A hierarchical hybrid sparsity codec is introduced to minimize data volume, significantly reducing external memory access. Moreover, a reconfigurable rulebook-GEMM fused spiking engine with flexible scheduling is developed to bridge the gap between fine-grained rulebook-based indexing and parallel execution, maintaining high performance across diverse sparsity distributions. The spike-based engine also secures low power consumption through discrete 1-bit data transmission and multiplier-free micro-architectural design. Fabricated in 28nm CMOS technology, the prototype chip achieves a peak system-level energy efficiency of 83.2 TOPS/W. Evaluation results show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art 3D point cloud processors with a 2.16x boost in energy efficiency and the least energy consumption per frame, making it highly suitable for edge intelligence.

item.title: A Low-Cost Trigonometric Current-Mode Phase Interpolator Exploiting the MOSFET Square-Law for Enhanced Phase Linearity
item.description: This paper presents a low-cost 7-bit current-mode phase interpolator (PI) with good linearity for high-speed clocking applications. Conventional current-mode PIs use a linear weighting strategy to produce a diamond-shaped phasor constellation in the I/Q plane, resulting in phase nonlinearity and code-dependent amplitude variation. Digital predistortion or lookup-table-based calibration improves the linearity but requires additional coefficient-generation or calibration hardware. The proposed PI employs a CML-based sin2/cos2 current-weighting scheme that exploits the square-law of the MOSFET. It drives the synthesized phasor closer to circular rotation in the analog domain, achieving a good trade-off among calibration complexity, coefficient-control overhead, and power consumption. Fabricated in a 40-nm CMOS process, the proposed PI occupies an active area of 0.015 mm2 and consumes 2.59 mW under a 1.1-V supply at 4 GHz. The measured differential nonlinearity (DNL) remains within ±1 LSB over the full code range, and the measured peak-to-peak integral nonlinearity (IN ${\mathrm{L}}_{\mathrm {pp}}$ ) is 1.37 LSB. The PI-added jitter is 72.1 fs over 10 kHz−1 GHz. These results demonstrate improved linearity while maintaining low power and compact area.

item.title: A Power-Efficient Timing-Aligned Charge-Injection Phase Rotator With Inherent Linearity for 64-Gb/s PAM-4 CDR
item.description: This paper presents a highly linear and power-efficient PR using the timing-aligned charge-injection technique. In the proposed PR, phase shifting is achieved by injecting charge into the oscillator core, and the phase step per injection is determined by the impulse sensitivity function (ISF). By controlling the number of injection cycles, the total phase shift is the accumulation of identical phase steps per injection, which makes the phase rotation inherently linear. Moreover, this architecture eliminates dedicated clock drivers by embedding the phase-tuning function inside the oscillator. It uses minimal charge per injection and is disabled after reaching the target phase, achieving negligible static power and low dynamic power. Consequently, the proposed PR avoids both the nonlinearity of conventional interpolation-based or integration-based designs and their associated power overhead. The proposed PR is implemented and verified in a 64-Gb/s reference-less PAM-4 CDR prototype fabricated in a 40-nm CMOS process. The PR core occupies an area of only $55\mu $ m $\times 25\mu $ m. It operates at 8 GHz with a power consumption of just 0.38 mW. Measurement results show a reconfigurable phase step ranging from 0.57° to 3.71° (equivalent to $6.6\sim 9.3$ -bit resolution) and an additive jitter of 115.8 fs. These results demonstrate that the proposed PR is well-suited for power-efficient, high-linearity CDR/PLL and other phase-modulation systems, offering a compelling combination of count-based PCW-to-phase linearity and ultra-low power consumption.

item.title: A Silicon-Based Integrated FMCW LiDAR System
item.description: This paper presents an integrated light detection and ranging (LiDAR) system alongside its corresponding 22-nm FD-SOI controller IC. The proposed architecture integrates four distinct dies—a 1550-nm DFB laser diode, a photonic IC (PIC), an $8\times 8$ silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) array, and a mixed-signal silicon controller chip—complemented by a custom resonant concave acoustic mechanical mirror specifically designed to support the multi-die assembly. A laser driver and stabilization electro-optic phase-locked loop (EO-PLL), transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs), variable gain amplifiers (VGAs), analog–to-digital converters (ADCs), a custom fast Fourier transform (FFT) engine, mirror drivers, SiPM read-out circuitry, power management and 8-Gbps low-voltage differential signaling (LVDS) driver are all integrated in planar double thick metal RF SOI process. The total final device volume target is less than 16 mm x 16 mm x 3.5 mm including the suspended mechanical concave mirror to be resonant driven from the same controller IC. A 20-mW 1550-nm distributed feedback (DFB) laser is to be flip coupled onto a 5mm x 10mm PIC along with the 4.8mm x 4.8mm SOI-CMOS die. Configured via a serial peripheral interface (SPI), the system directly transfers processed FFT data to the host processor through multiple high-speed interfaces, rendering it highly viable for cost-constrained embedded applications. The maximum system bandwidth is 4-GHz (8-GSPS 4-interleaved ADCs) with various reconfigurable chirp and ramp rates and it is designed to continuously stream out maximum throughput of 8-Gbps through source synchronous LVDS link. The digital signal processing (DSP) backend in auto-chirp mode can dynamically adjust the chirp period and chirp slope for optimal range resolution.

item.title: A 96.7%-Peak-Efficiency 2.5-A Scalable Hybrid Buck Converter Module With Complementary Dual-Mode Reconfiguration and Interleaving-Assisted COUT Augmentation
item.description: This article presents a scalable hybrid DC-DC converter module for compact CPU/GPU power delivery. The proposed complementary dual-mode reconfigurable topology combines two extended dual-path switched-capacitor cells through a DEMUX path, enabling a continuous 0.4–1.5-V output from a 1.8-V input while maintaining full-range inductor-current reduction. The overlapping voltage-conversion-ratio (VCR) regions avoid extremely narrow duty ratios near the mode boundary and support smooth hot switching, with a current capability enhancement factor ( $I_{\mathrm {LOAD}}$ / $I_{\mathrm {L,DC}}$ ) of 1.33–2 over the targeted range. An N-phase interleaving scheme further exploits the phase in which the flying capacitor is paralleled with the output capacitor, thereby enhancing the globally equivalent output capacitance and reducing both output ripple and flying-capacitor hard-charging stress. A fully integrated gate-driver scheme with a shared charge pump and bootstrap capacitor reduces off-chip components, while a $V^{2}I_{\mathrm {L}}$ adaptive-on-time controller improves transient recovery. Fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS process, the prototype integrates the power stage, drivers, and controller in 4.86 mm2. A single module achieves 96.7% peak efficiency and 2.5 A maximum load, and a four-module interleaved prototype delivers 10 A with 96% peak efficiency using a 94.7%-reduced global output capacitor.

item.title: A Dual-Triggered Adaptive-Cycle SIMO Buck-Boost Converter With Hybrid Zero-Current Detector for Thermoelectric Energy Harvesting
item.description: This paper presents a buck-boost converter with dual-triggered adaptive-cycle (DTAC) control for thermoelectric energy harvesting. The proposed DTAC control dynamically determines the switching period according to the energy conditions at both the input and output nodes, while adaptively adjusting the on-time based on the input energy condition to maintain the energy extraction point close to the maximum power point. Based on a single-inductor multiple-output (SIMO) architecture, the converter regulates two output voltages with the assistance of an energy storage capacitor, $C_{\text {STO}}$ , which recovers the residual inductor energy during the discharge phase. In addition, a low-power hybrid zero-current detector (H-ZCD) is implemented to accurately detect the inductor zero-current point. The proposed converter was fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS process with an active area of 0.701 mm2. Measurement results show that the converter operates over an input voltage range of 0.1–0.5 V and supports a load power range of 0.01–6.6 mW. It achieves a peak conversion efficiency of 85.3%, while the use of $C_{\text {STO}}$ reduces the output voltage ripple by up to 40%. The implemented H-ZCD consumes only 800 nW.

item.title: A Wide-Load High-Stability LDO With Dynamic Semi-Pole Compensation and Capacitor Tracking Technique
item.description: A low-dropout regulator (LDO) exhibiting an extended load range is presented, wherein both wide load resistance and capacitance ranges are simultaneously achieved. Whereas conventional compensation schemes are restricted to stable operation over a narrow load resistance interval at a specific capacitance value. To overcome the limited load range, a dynamic semi-pole compensation (DSPC) in conjunction with a capacitor tracking technique (CTT) is proposed. Consequently, stable operation is ensured over a load resistance span of $20~\Omega $ to 10 M $\Omega $ and a load capacitance range of $1~\mu $ F to $200~\mu $ F. The design is implemented in a 0.18- $\mu $ m process. An input voltage range of 3.6–40 V is supported, with a regulated output voltage of 3.3 V and a maximum load current of 150 mA. The dropout voltage is measured to be 270 mV. A power-supply rejection ratio (PSRR) of 60 dB at 10 kHz is attained. The load regulation is $24~\mu $ V/mA, and the line regulation is 0.017 mV/V. A quiescent current of $2.9~\mu $ A is consumed under no-load operation.

item.title: QUARC: A Compact and Energy-Efficient Quad-Mode Reconfigurable Analog--Digital Hybrid eDRAM CIM for Ternary-LLM Acceleration
item.description: This paper presents QUARC, a highly energy-efficient analog–digital hybrid computing-in-memory (CIM) processor for ternary large language model (LLM) acceleration. QUARC leverages a high-density 3T1C embedded DRAM bitcell and introduces a quad-mode reconfigurable macro with causal-mask-adaptive operation to improve both macro- and system-level energy efficiency. The proposed architecture incorporates four key features. First, a sign-embedded ternary encoding scheme supports both ternary projection and multi-bit attention, enabling area-efficient analog MAC operations. Second, an in-column signed-magnitude SAR ADC reduces ADC area overhead by up to 87.5% and lowers ADC energy consumption by up to 82% through comparison skipping. Third, in-column partial-sum accumulation exploits in-memory digital computation to process only effective bits, reducing accumulation area and energy by 90.5% and 91%, respectively. Fourth, causal-mask-adaptive pipelining dynamically scales with the linearly increasing attention workload and eliminates redundant KV re-computations that can incur up to a $30\times $ overhead. Implemented in a 28 nm CMOS process, the proposed CIM processor achieves a macro cell density of 1.91 Mb/mm2 and peak macro energy efficiencies of 390 TOPS/W and 48.2 TOPS/W for ternary projection and multi-bit attention, respectively. It also achieves system energy efficiency of 101.4 TOPS/W while maintaining a perplexity of 11.9 on WikiText-2 with 1.3B ternary-LLM.

item.title: A Single-Mode Hybrid Buck--Boost Converter for Voltage-Regulating Cable in Cell-to-Cell Power Delivery System
item.description: This paper presents a hybrid buck–boost converter for a voltage-regulating cable enabling cell-to-cell (C2C) power delivery (PD) for identical cell counts. An inductor-first architecture directly utilizes the cable inductance as the energy-transfer element, achieving single-mode step-up/down operation over a wide conversion ratio (CR) range suitable for single-cell C2C PD. Power-stage loss is minimized by reducing both voltage and current stress on the switches. Unlike conventional non-inverting buck–boost converters, the output current is continuously delivered through multiple current paths, which mitigates the right-half-plane (RHP) zero and enables stable voltage regulation without requiring an additional current-control loop. Fabricated in a $0.18~\mu $ m BCD process, the proposed VRC converter achieves a peak chip efficiency of 95.6 % and maintains efficiency above 91.5 % across the entire target VIN–VO operating range in USB type-C cable power delivery, with a passive component volume of 0.75 mm3.

item.title: A Timing Relaxed Pre-Decision Feedforward Equalizer for DSP-Based Wireline Receiver Using Hardware-in-the-Loop Verification on FPGA
item.description: This paper presents a critical-timing-relaxed pre-decision feedforward equalizer (pDFFE) designed for high-speed digital signal processor (DSP)-based wireline receivers. Since conventional decision feedback equalizer (DFE) suffers from an increasing timing burden due to recursive feedback loops, which hinder parallelization and scalability, the proposed pDFFE architecture eliminates the feedback path by replacing post-cursor inter-symbol interference (ISI) cancellation with feed-forward equalizer (FFE)-based decisions. The overall system employs a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) verification platform based on the Versal ACAP, integrating a DSP engine with sign-sign LMS (SS-LMS) adaptation. The power and area of the proposed DSP in 28 nm CMOS layout are estimated to be 176.5 mW and 0.201 mm2, respectively. Both simulation and measurement results under −24 dB channel loss at Nyquist frequency demonstrate reliable BER performance comparable to the conventional DFE, while achieving single-clock latency and improving area efficiency, from a minimum of 10 % to a maximum of 47 %, compared to conventional architectures.

item.title: KWS-CIM: A Charge-Domain eDRAM-Based Compute-in-Memory Macro for Ternary DFSMN Keyword Spotting
item.description: This paper presents a 3T2C embedded DRAM (eDRAM)-based charge-domain compute-in-memory (CIM) macro for ternary deep feedforward sequential memory network (DFSMN)-based keyword spotting (KWS) with ternary activations and binary weights. The proposed architecture integrates a charge-domain ternary multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) bitcell, a selectable dual-mode sensing scheme, and an in-array offset calibration technique using fixed calibration rows. The dual-mode sensing scheme supports an energy-prioritized conventional sense amplifier (SA) mode for always-on monitoring and an accuracy-prioritized two-step sense amplifier (TSSA) mode for robust inference under reduced sensing margins. The proposed TSSA mitigates decision-timing-induced kickback disturbance, while the calibration rows suppress systematic column-wise sensing offsets. A sense amplifier-based 1-bit readout is employed to minimize area overhead. Fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS process, the proposed macro operates up to 250 MHz and achieves 930–1335 TOPS/W in the conventional SA mode and 82–336 TOPS/W in the TSSA mode, with an area efficiency of 18.45 TOPS/mm2. For DFSMN-based KWS, the measured accuracies with the calibrated TSSA mode reach 91.66%, 89.87%, and 87.30% for the 12-, 20-, and 35-class KWS settings (CLS12, CLS20, and CLS35), respectively. Additional evaluations achieve 98.02% on MNIST and 87.32% on CIFAR-10 with ResNet18, demonstrating the general applicability of the proposed eDRAM CIM macro.

item.title: A 920-MS/s 12-bit Energy-Efficient SAR-Assisted Pipelined ADC With a Dynamic-Bias Floating Ring Amplifier
item.description: This paper presents a 12-bit SAR-assisted pipelined ADC that features an energy-efficient self-biasing amplifier. Based on a unified architecture-level power model, we identify the 3-3-3-6-bit resolution partition as an energy-efficient solution for gigahertz ADCs. The proposed amplifier employs a floating power supply with a compact adaptive gate-biasing scheme to improve high-frequency stability without consuming static bias current. An output-dependent feedback-compensation further enhances linearity without extra circuits, flattening the gain versus output voltage characteristic over a wide output swing. Moreover, a low-latency SAR logic switching scheme improves timing efficiency without hardware overhead, allocating more time for accurate residue-amplifier settling and thereby achieving an optimal balance between speed and accuracy. With these techniques, a single-channel 12-bit SAR-assisted pipelined ADC, fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, achieves 9.15-bit ENOB and 68.8-dB SFDR at 920 MS/s with a near-Nyquist input. Operating from a 1-V supply, the ADC consumes 13.2 mW, resulting in a Walden FoM of 25.3 fJ/conv.-step.

item.title: System-Level Modeling and Implementation of Spread-Spectrum Clocking in a Multi-Channel PMIC With RB-ACOT DC--DC Converters
item.description: This paper proposes and validates the implementation of a Spread-Spectrum Clocking (SSC) technique in a fully-integrated 6-channel Power Management Integrated Circuit (PMIC) for power management applications of microprocessor units. Each channel of the PMIC embeds a Ripple-Based Adaptive Constant ON-Time (RB-ACOT) DC–DC Buck converter and a type-II Charge-Pump Phase-Locked Loop (CP-PLL). The converters are synchronized via the CP-PLLs to mutually phase-shifted reference clock signals derived from a centralized SSC-modulated reference oscillator. We investigate here from a theoretical perspective the impact of the CP-PLL in altering the effectiveness of the SSC technique through a design-oriented model that includes both the CP-PLL and the RB-ACOT converter. A prototype of the proposed system is fabricated in 0.18-um Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) process. Both simulation results and experimental measurements demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution in mitigating the conducted electromagnetic interference level generated by the PMIC, achieving up to 12 dB of attenuation.

item.title: A 1.1-GHz Tuning Range, High-Linearity, Power- and Area-Efficient Ring Oscillator for VCO-Based ADCs in FMCW LiDARs
item.description: Voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO)-based analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) are potentially advantageous for modern and next-generation automotive LiDARs due to their low power (<2-mW) and small IC area (<0.01-mm2). Nevertheless, state-of-the-art VCOs require linearization techniques that either incur power and area overheads or suffer from limited tuning range ( $\ll 1$ -GHz), thereby compromising the ADC resolution. We present herein a power- and area-efficient ring-oscillator-based VCO embodying two novel linearization techniques applied to the transconductor and to the delay-cell. The first technique employs a proposed transistor network to dynamically vary the degeneration resistance according to the input voltage, thereby linearizing the transconductor. The second technique exploits the propagation delay of a level shifter within the proposed linearized delay-cell to compensate for the non-linearity of the conventional delay-cell. We derive analytical expressions for both techniques to identify the mechanisms that influence the VCO linearity and verify them through post-layout simulations. Finally, we perform measurements on a prototype IC embodying the two proposed techniques. The proposed VCO achieves a low non-linearity error of 1.68% over a 1.1-GHz range, while consuming 80- $\mu $ W and occupying a compact area of 120- $\mu $ m2. We also propose a figure-of-merit and on this basis, we show that the proposed VCO surpasses the state-of-the-art by $11\times $ .

item.title: A High-Throughput FPGA Accelerator for Real-Time Sort-Free 3-D Gaussian Splatting
item.description: This paper presents the first FPGA-based real-time sort-free 3DGS accelerator through algorithm–architecture co-optimization. The accelerator enables a fully pipelined and highly parallel rendering architecture by eliminating global depth sorting and adopting an order-independent weighted-sum accumulation scheme. The proposed Gaussian pruning scheme further reduces the number of Gaussian primitives by 64%–80% with less than 1.35 dB PSNR loss while maintaining over 30 dB PSNR. Spherical harmonics analysis is applied to facilitate hardware design for rendering quality and hardware complexity balancing. A scale-adaptive Covariance Computation Unit is designed to remove data overflow for stable computation. An optimized Width Predictor and Processing Element further reduce the redundant computation and the rendering latency by 57.5%. Implemented on an AMD-Xilinx Alveo U200 FPGA, the proposed accelerator achieves 637.6 FPS while consuming only 2.7 W at 60 MHz. Compared with prior FPGA-based rendering accelerators, this work achieves $4.77\times $ – $7.97\times $ better energy efficiency, demonstrating an efficient and scalable solution for real-time 3DGS rendering on edge computing platforms.

item.title: A ±50-A Shunt-Based Current Sensor With ±0.2% Gain Error From --40 °C to 125 °C
item.description: This paper presents a shunt-based low-side current sensor that consists of an off-chip PCB trace shunt resistor and a readout circuit. A temperature-dependent reference voltage, composed of a proportional-to-absolute-temperature voltage and a tunable complementary-to-absolute-temperature (CTAT) voltage, is used to compensate for the shunt’s temperature-dependent resistance variation. To compensate for both the first- and higher-order temperature dependence of the shunt resistor, this paper proposes a CTAT voltage generation technique based on a temperature-coefficient (TC)-adjustable current source and a CTAT resistor. This technique enables the shunt’s temperature-dependent resistance variation to be compensated over a wide temperature range using only a single batch-calibration parameter. In addition, this paper proposes a dual-mode amplifier for the first integrator of the discrete-time $\Delta \Sigma $ ADC-based readout circuit to improve power efficiency and reduce sensitivity to PVT variation. The current sensor was fabricated in a 0.18- $\mu $ m CMOS process occupying 0.43 mm2 and consumes $374~\mu $ W from a 1.8-V supply. Over the automotive temperature range ( $- 40~^{\circ }$ C to $125~^{\circ }$ C) and for currents up to ±50 A, it achieves a gain error of ±0.2% after a one-point gain trim at room temperature.

item.title: An Area-Efficient Synthesizable Inverter-Delay-Ring Time-to-Digital Converter With Enhanced Linearity
item.description: A fully synthesizable, area-optimized time-to-digital converter (TDC) with improved linearity is described. Its architecture exploits a cyclic inverter-based delay line (ring) tapped with two alternating cycle counters. A compact delay ring enables reduced hardware cost and efficient digital post-processing. The delay ring linearity is enhanced through back-annotated insertion of optional dummy inverter capacitive loads. To estimate the average inverter propagation delay, a straightforward calibration scheme is proposed. The TDC prototype fabricated in 180 nm CMOS occupies 4500 $\mu $ m2 and consumes a mean power of 2.7 mW at 1.8 V and room temperature. It achieves 52 ps resolution over a 3.2 ns full-scale range, with maximum DNL/INL of 0.38/0.7 LSB and measured single-shot precision of up to 16 ps or 0.31 LSB. Due to its low complexity, excellent PPA, and automated standard-cell-based implementation, the presented architecture is suitable for applications that require numerous digital timing channels.

item.title: A Two-Unit-Interval Window Oversampling Referenceless Clock and Data Recovery for Robust Frequency Detection Against Duty-Cycle Distortion of Received Data
item.description: This paper proposes a reference-less clock and data recovery (CDR) architecture that employs two-unit-interval (2-UI) windowing for frequency acquisition. The proposed 2-UI-based frequency detector (FD) enables half-rate frequency tracking without frequency-detection errors even in the presence of duty-cycle distortion (DCD) in the received data. Conventional Extended Bang-Bang Phase Detector (XBBPD) suffers from sampling errors near data transition edges due to variations in the reference interval for frequency detection. This results in false frequency-up/down (FUP/FDN) signals and may lead to prolonged stabilization time. Moreover, conventional XBBPD-based FD requires careful tuning of the FLL gain and lock-detection tolerance to avoid false lock or lock release under DCD. To address these limitations, the proposed FD employs six sampling points over a 2-UI window, effectively avoiding DCD-affected regions while maintaining a constant reference interval, thereby reducing the probability of mis-detections during frequency tracking. The prototype, fabricated in a 28-nm FD-SOI process, tolerates up to 11% duty-cycle distortion without frequency detection errors. The proposed reference-less CDR achieves a minimum lock time of $1.5\mu $ s and an energy efficiency of 1.57 pJ/bit at 14 Gb/s.

item.title: SPAHRTA: Sparsity-Aware Hybrid Run-Time Training Accelerator for Spiking Neural Networks
item.description: Training Spiking Vision Transformers (SViTs) on heterogeneous accelerators faces two compounding inefficiencies: backwards locking from conventional backpropagation prevents sparse and dense cores from operating concurrently, and spatio-temporal activation sparsity makes compile-time workload allocation suboptimal across training. We present SPAHRTA, a co-designed acceleration stack that addresses both through complementary training-algorithm and runtime-allocation mechanisms on a heterogeneous SNN-DNN SoC. The algorithmic contribution pairs Hybrid-DFA—which selectively replaces backpropagation in MLP sub-blocks with Direct Feedback Alignment—with an Out-of-Sync schedule that overlaps the forward and backward passes of successive mini-batches. The runtime contribution, Dynamic Workload Allocation (DWA), tracks per-dispatch sparsity and adaptively splits each operation across the sparse and dense cores. SPAHRTA realizes both mechanisms on a 4.23 mm2 SoC at TSMC 28nm post-synthesis (1.024 TFLOPS peak at 500 MHz), with sparse cores using shift-based zero-skipping and dense cores using native UINT2FP cross-type bridging. The contributions address different parts of the training stack: h-DFA+OoS exposes cross-minibatch overlap, and DWA maps the overlapped work to sparse and dense cores. Together, they achieve a combined speedup that is $1.30\times $ larger than the product of their isolated gains. SPAHRTA delivers $2.22\times $ – $2.30\times $ end-to-end Spikformer training speedup over conventional backpropagation without DWA on CIFAR-100 with a 1.76 pp Top-1 accuracy drop and a 29% subsystem energy-delay product reduction.

item.title: A Single-Mode Double Step-Up-Down Hybrid Converter With Reduced Inductor Current and Continuous Output Current
item.description: This paper presents a double step-up-down (DSUD) hybrid converter with single-mode operation, designed for lithium-ion battery applications in mobile devices. By employing solitary $D$ -control, the converter achieves seamless buck and boost operations without mode transitions, allowing output voltage to be seamlessly adjusted to the target voltage. With the inductors permanently connected to the output, the inductor current is always equal to half of the load current, thereby reducing inductor DCR losses and power transistors conduction losses. Furthermore, it achieves continuous output current delivery, which minimizes output voltage ripple and eliminates the right-half-plane zero. Additionally, the introduction of adaptive ramp circuit with fast path improves the transient response, while the proposed dual-stage start-up circuit eliminates inrush current and allows the converter to gradually reach the steady-state. The proposed DSUD converter was fabricated using a 0.18- $\mu $ m BCD process. The chip is designed to deliver a regulated 3.3 V output with a maximum load current of 1 A from an input voltage ranging from 2.7 V to 4.2 V. Measured results show an output voltage ripple of less than 12 mV and a peak efficiency of 96.9%, achieved with $4.7~\mu $ H inductors, $2.2~\mu $ F output capacitor, and switching frequency of 1 MHz.

item.title: A 410-MHz Bandwidth and 22.7-dBm OIP3 dB-Linear Variable Gain Active-RC Feedback Amplifier With High Frequency Feedforward Compensated OTA and Ramp-Based Control
item.description: This paper presents a dB-linear variable gain amplifier (VGA) based on an active-RC feedback filter topology with a ramp-based control scheme. As a core building block of a closed-loop amplifier-based VGA, a self-biased current-reuse feedforward (FF) compensated operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) is incorporated. The proposed FF-OTA achieves a unity-gain bandwidth (UGB) of 2.92 GHz and a DC gain of 36.25 dB while consuming only 3.1 mW. To ensure smooth gain scaling, our proposed VGA incorporates a tunable ramp-based control that eliminates discrete steps typically introduced by switched-resistor transitions. This approach enables stable dB-linear operation and yields highly linear performance, achieving an OIP3 of 22.7 dBm at the highest gain setting, outperforming conventional open-loop VGAs. Owing to the ramp generator’s flexibility, the VGA supports a wide 0.5 V control range and achieves an effective dB-linear region spanning 25 dB within a total gain range of 28 dB, with a 0.4 dB gain error. The prototype circuit, based on a single-stage active-RC filter, operates at a constant bandwidth of 410 MHz, and the VGA core draws 6 mW from a 1.2 V supply. Fabricated using TSMC 65 nm CMOS technology, the VGA occupies a compact core area of 0.037 mm2.

item.title: T-2T SRAM: A CMOS 8-bit T-2T SRAM Ladder-Based Analog Current-Domain Compute-in-Memory (CIM) Architecture
item.description: This paper presents a CMOS 8-bit T-2T SRAM ladder-based analog current-domain Compute-In-Memory (CIM) architecture for multi-bit neural network applications. A 1-to-2 ratio CMOS 8-bit T-2T SRAM ladder structure was implemented across the entire Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) macro, where the area scales linearly (~N) with N-weight, while the power consumption scales sub-linearly (~2(1 - 1 / $2{^{\text {N-1}}}$ ), enabling area- and power-efficient multi-bit CIM operation. The proposed T-2T SRAM ladder-based Successive Approximation Register Analog-to-Digital Converter (SAR ADC) effectively reuses the memory read and write peripheral circuits for asynchronous SAR operation, removing the need for dedicated SAR logic and register, thereby improving silicon area efficiency. Pre-distortion technique was implemented within input Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) stage, to compensate for the non-linearities within the Synaptic T-2T bitcells. The proposed T-2T SRAM architecture exhibits PVT tolerance through an inherent differential tracking and compensation mechanism between the main and reference computing paths, effectively suppressing PVT-induced variations and preserving MAC linearity. Fabricated using TSMC 65nm GP CMOS process, the proposed T-2T SRAM chip achieved a peak energy efficiency of 4.99 TOPS/W, a peak throughput of 1.5 GOPS/Kb, and a peak compute density of 0.114 TOPS/mm2. Using the hardware-aware neural network analysis framework, we achieved 92.11% classification accuracy on the CIFAR-10 dataset with a VGG-9 model, and 67.43%/90.28% Top-1/Top-5 accuracy on the CIFAR-100 dataset with a ResNet-20 model.

item.title: A 128 × 128 Dual-Resolution CMOS Image Sensor With In-Sensor Temporal and Spatial Gradient Calculations for Optical Flow Pre-Processing
item.description: This paper presents a $128\times 128$ smart CMOS image sensor that utilizes the processing-in-sensor (PIS) technique for gradient-based pyramidal optical flow pre-processing in power- and bandwidth-constrained edge vision systems. By embedding motion feature extraction directly within the image sensor, the proposed design avoids complex computation and frequent frame-buffer access in digital processors. The sensor simultaneously outputs temporal gradients, two-dimensional spatial gradients, raw intensity images, and dual-resolution data within a single frame period. A multi-row access readout scheme enables concurrent availability of neighboring pixel data, while column-level time-domain processing circuits efficiently compute spatial gradients and $3\times 3$ binning without relying on power-hungry analog subtraction or extensive digital buffering. Fabricated in TSMC 0.18- $\mu $ m standard CMOS process, the prototype sensor operates at $198.44~\mu $ W at 30 fps. Measurement results demonstrate accurate gradient and binning outputs, with root-mean-square errors of 0.4 LSB for spatial gradients and 1.6 LSB for binned images (8-bit). Using the measured gradients, off-chip optical flow computation achieves an end-point error of 0.375 pixel, and the proposed binning-based pyramidal scheme extends the detectable motion range by approximately three times. The proposed vision sensor achieves an iFoM of 0.1971pJ/pixel $\cdot $ frame $\cdot $ level, validating the effectiveness of the proposed PIS-based architecture for motion-aware edge vision applications.

item.title: A 135-FPS and 0.81-mJ/frame Heterogeneous Processor for Real-Time and Energy-Efficient LiDAR Odometry and Mapping
item.description: The growing demand for physical AI is expanding the capabilities of autonomous systems; however, these capabilities require accurate trajectory estimation and precise 3D map reconstruction for understanding the surrounding environment. In this context, LiDAR Odometry and Mapping (LOAM) has gained attention as a widely adopted SLAM framework that offers dense geometric map reconstruction. Nevertheless, the large number of keypoints captured per frame makes real-time hardware acceleration of LOAM extremely challenging in mobile robots, and even high-performance CPUs/GPUs fail to meet real-time constraints. This paper presents a real-time and energy-efficient heterogeneous processor with four key architectural features to address the dominant memory and computational bottlenecks of LOAM acceleration: 1) a 3D spherical-bin partitioning with neighboring bin search tailored to LiDAR point distributions, reducing the number of comparisons by 99.6%; 2) a hash-page-based memory management unit that lowers the required on-chip memory capacity by 96.9% through prediction-based dynamic memory allocation exploiting spatio-temporal coherence; 3) a neighboring-bin cache that achieves a $10.5\times $ improvement in kNN energy efficiency by reducing redundant memory accesses and increasing PE utilization; and 4) a reconfigurable non-linear optimization core that shortens NLO latency by 92.3% through multi-level computational parallelization. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, the proposed processor achieves 36.9 ms latency and 0.81 mJ/frame energy consumption, demonstrating its capability for real-time LOAM acceleration in mobile systems.

item.title: A 28-nm 2.25-Mb CO-DCIM RRAM Macro With 1.25-ns/bit Read Speed, 0.12-pJ/bit, and 12.85-Mb/mm2 Storage Density for Autoregressive Transformer
item.description: Edge AI urgently demand computing hardware with large on-chip storage capacity, low memory access overhead. Resistive random-access memory (RRAM) based digital computing-in-memory (DCIM) suits such scenarios by achieving a optimized performance balance in calculation precision, storage density and access overhead. However, traditional RRAM-DCIM scheme suffers from two issues: 1) RRAM multi-bit storage boosts density but introduces significant errors, while conventional ECC scheme requires massive redundant bits that offset density gains; 2) Wiring RC parasitism in large-scale arrays leads to slow and energy-intensive random access. To resolve these issues, the proposed computation-oriented DCIM (CO-DCIM) paradigm integrates two core solutions: a hierarchical multi-bit storage coding scheme and a charge-domain continuous access scheme. The designed CO-DCIM macro is fabricated in a 28nm CMOS technology. Measurement results show a single RRAM read latency of 2.5 ns, normalized read energy of 0.12 pJ/bit, and a storage density of 12.85 Mb/mm2. The macro is further evaluated on public SimpleAR-0.5B-RL and SimpleAR-1.5B-RL workloads, showing a 29.2x reduction in mapped-weight access energy relative to LPDDR5X DRAM at $256\times 256$ resolution.

item.title: A 65-nm Compute-in-Read-Only-Memory Macro With Bidirectional Ternary Weight Storage and Sparsity-Aware Local Accumulation for 1.58-bit LLM Inference
item.description: Compute-in-Read-Only-Memory (CiROM) is a promising paradigm for weight reload-free edge inference. The recent emergence of BitNet, which represents weights in ternary values at an average precision of approximately 1.58 bits, opens a path toward single-chip LLM deployment by drastically reducing storage footprint. However, fully exploiting this opportunity requires addressing three key challenges: compact ternary weight storage, effective exploitation of high weight sparsity, and post-fabrication adaptability for downstream tasks. To this end, this paper presents a BitNet-oriented CiROM macro with three dedicated techniques. First, a Bidirectional ROM Array based on Configurable Source/Bit-Lines stores two ternary weights in each 1T ROM cell, significantly improving the weight storage density. Second, a Tri-Mode Local Accumulator is developed to support an accumulation-then-summation dataflow, where zero-weight operations are locally gated to translate BitNet sparsity into reduced switching activity and energy consumption. Third, a lightweight digital adapter co-designed with LoRA-based fine-tuning is introduced to provide post-fabrication downstream task adaptability with negligible hardware overhead. The proposed macro is fabricated in a 65nm CMOS process and achieves an ultra-high weight bit density of 4,479 Kb/mm2, corresponding to an $9.20\times $ improvement over prior digital CiROM designs. Silicon measurements demonstrate a peak energy efficiency of 33.7 TOPS/W and a peak compute density of 60.8 GOPS/mm2 over a 0.6-1.2 V supply range. Model-level evaluations further confirm that the proposed digital adapter consistently improves downstream performance across diverse tasks. These results demonstrate that the proposed macro extends CiROM toward efficient weight reload-free LLM acceleration, providing a promising path for compact and energy-efficient edge deployment.

item.title: High-Precision Low-Complexity Method and Architecture for Computing Sigmoid and Tanh Functions
item.description: The sigmoid and tanh activation functions are extensively used in gated recurrent neural networks for state updates and gating operations. Compared with inference, neural network training imposes much stricter requirements on the numerical precision of activation functions. Therefore, we present a radix-4 CORDIC-based architecture for the first time for computing the sigmoid and tanh activation functions. Compared with standard radix-2 CORDIC, the radix-4 CORDIC reduces the number of iterations by half, thereby improving computational speed while maintaining high precision. To extend the input range, we introduce an activation function base-change strategy that replaces the natural base with base 2. By requiring only high-precision exponential computation over a small input range, the proposed method is able to handle inputs of arbitrary magnitude, reducing the overall computational complexity. In hardware implementation, experimental results demonstrate mean absolute errors of $1.62\times 10^{-5}$ and $3.14\times 10^{-5}$ for the base-2 sigmoid and tanh functions, respectively, compared with exact functions. Moreover, the pipelined hardware implementation achieves reductions of 27.05% in area, 35.87% in power consumption, and 43.75% in latency, compared with the radix-2 CORDIC architecture, further demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

item.title: Shuffle-CIM-NR: From Shuffle-Based All-Analog Inference to Noise-Resilient Charge-Domain Computing-in-Memory for Near-Sensor Intelligence
item.description: Near-sensor smart sensing requires compact and energy-efficient hardware to support local deep neural network (DNN) inference under stringent power, latency, and accuracy constraints. Analog compute-in-memory (ACIM) exploits analog-domain multiply-accumulate (MAC) to improve computing density and energy efficiency, making it a promising hardware solution for low-power near-sensor smart sensing. However, existing ACIM architectures still suffer from two major limitations for near-sensor deployment: the power and latency overhead caused by cross-bank partial-sum (pSUM) accumulation and digital-domain non-MAC operations, and the computation accuracy degradation induced by analog circuit non-idealities. This brief presents Shuffle-CIM-NR, a shuffle-based charge-domain CIM architecture for low-power and robust near-sensor inference. By mapping shuffled convolution groups into individual CIM banks, Shuffle-CIM-NR eliminates cross-bank pSUM accumulation and enables one-shot 4-bit signed-weight/activation MAC operations. To further improve analog computing robustness, Shuffle-CIM-NR co-optimizes the activation input path, signed multi-bit MAC computation, and analog readout, while integrating batch-normalization (BN), activation, and quantization into the ADC. Implemented in TSMC 22-nm CMOS, the proposed architecture achieves an energy efficiency of 283.2 TOPS/W and an area efficiency of 2.73 TOPS/mm2 with excellent linearity, providing an efficient and robust CIM solution for near-sensor smart sensing applications.

item.title: A 6T--11T In-Memory Computing Architecture for Near-Sensor Pipelined Binary Neural Network
item.description: This brief presents the fabrication and experimental validation of an interlaced 6T-11T CMOS in-memory computing circuit designed for low-silicon-area pipelined binary neural networks. The circuit implements a weight-stationary architecture in which input activation values are sequentially stored in 6T SRAM columns, while 11T cells retain the convolution weights and perform binary XNOR-based multiply-and-accumulate operations, naturally aligning with the column-parallel readout topology of CMOS image sensors. The circuit has been fabricated in a 180 nm standard CMOS process and experimentally characterized. Measured results on a binary convolutional layer demonstrate operation at 1 MHz with a simulation-assisted energy efficiency of 18.53 TOPS/W. The interlaced organization embeds the line-buffer functionality required for streamed convolution within the IMC array itself, so that image rows are processed as they are read out from the sensor.

item.title: A Heterogeneously Integrated Balanced Doherty Power Amplifier With Reconfigurable Adaptive Bias for 5G-Advanced Power Class 1 Terminals
item.description: This paper presents a heterogeneously integrated balanced voltage-combined Doherty power amplifier (DPA) for 5G-Advanced n77 power class 1 terminals. A reconfigurable adaptive bias technique is employed in the peaking amplifier to enhance broadband linearity. In addition, a compact transformer-based quadrature coupler is developed as the input splitter and output combiner, realizing an area-efficient balanced architecture with inherent load mismatch resilience. The fabricated DPA operates from 3.3 to 4.2 GHz and achieves more than 39 dBm saturated output power over a 24% fractional bandwidth while occupying only 1.27 mm2 of GaAs HBT area. Under a 100-MHz 5G NR signal, it delivers 34 dBm linear output power with power-added efficiency (PAE) exceeding 40% and adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) better than −40 dBc without digital predistortion.

item.title: A Frequency-Reconfigurable Single-Stage Analog Linearizer for Joint AM–AM and AM–PM Compensation in Wideband PAs
item.description: Conventional analog predistortion techniques typically address amplitude and phase nonlinearity separately, often incurring a narrow operating frequency range. This brief presents a frequency-reconfigurable single-stage analog linearizer (SSAL) that jointly compensates for both amplitude and phase nonlinearities over a broad frequency coverage, using only a single transformer. The SSAL integrates diode-connected transistors with a nonlinear inductor, enabling simultaneous amplitude-to-amplitude (AM-AM) and amplitude-to-phase (AM-PM) correction in a compact circuitry. Moreover, the switchable transistor arrays are introduced to extend the operating frequency range and enhance linearization performance. Prototyped in 65-nm CMOS with a wideband PA, the proposed SSAL shows significant linearity improvement over a broad frequency range. The measurements reveal that the output power at $P_{\text {1dB}}$ (OP1dB) is improved by 3.4/3.9/3.1 dB to 16.6/17.8/16.5 dBm and the power added efficiency (PAE) at $P_{\text {1dB}}$ is increased by 9.5/12.8/8.9% to 22.1/28.8/22.5% at 25/30/35 GHz. The error vector magnitude (EVM) is decreased from 6.9/7.1/7.1% to 3.4/3.4/3.4% at 27/30/33 GHz under a 400 MHz 256-QAM OFDM signal.

item.title: Automated Synthesis of Multi-Frequency MMIC Matching Networks via Neural Dynamic Programming
item.description: This brief presents a neural dynamic programming (NDP) framework for the automated synthesis of MMIC matching networks. Given complex source and load impedances over multiple frequency points, we formulate the synthesis objective as maximizing the product of the transducer power gains ( $\boldsymbol {G_{\textbf {T}}}$ ) of the matching network, or equivalently, the sum of $\boldsymbol {G_{\textbf {T}}}$ in dB. To address the combinatorial optimization arising from multi-element cascaded topologies, the synthesis is reformulated as a dynamic programming problem. A sequence of neural networks is trained to recursively synthesize the matching network with one element at a time. The proposed NDP framework is implemented in a commercial GaAs process and validated through a set of four-element matching-network synthesis experiments. Compared with a genetic algorithm, the proposed method achieves an average improvement of 0.74 dB in $\boldsymbol {G_{\textbf {T}}}$ product while reducing the synthesis time from 35 s to 0.5 s.

item.title: Energy-Efficient Approximate Multipliers Based on Error-Compensating Approximate Adders
item.description: This work presents energy-efficient approximate multipliers based on two complementary types of approximate adders, one that underestimates and another that overestimates the result of addition. Owing to their simplified logic structures, these adders significantly reduce hardware cost. The main strength of the proposed approach lies in exploiting the complementary error behavior of these adders. When strategically placed within the partial product reduction stage of an approximate multiplier, their opposing error tendencies enable effective error compensation, resulting in a favorable balance between accuracy and hardware efficiency. Applying these adders to 8–11 least significant columns of an 8-bit multiplier yields substantial hardware improvements, including up to 53% reduction in delay, 82% reduction in energy consumption, and 76% reduction in area, while maintaining mean relative error distance (MRED) values between 3.4% and 12.1%. For similar accuracy levels, the proposed multipliers consistently outperform state-of-the-art approximate multipliers in terms of delay, power, and area. The architecture is scalable, allowing larger bit-width multipliers to be constructed iteratively from smaller configurations, with increasing hardware benefits observed at higher bit-widths for comparable normalized error levels. This work further evaluates the proposed multipliers in practical applications, including deep neural networks and image processing. When integrated into the fine-tuned ViT-Small vision transformer model, the design incurs only a 0.1% reduction in classification accuracy while achieving 37% energy and 40% area savings compared to an exact multiplier. Image multiplication and Sobel edge detection experiments also demonstrate high output quality, with PSNR and SSIM values exceeding 30 dB and 0.9, respectively.

item.title: An Energy-Efficient Sparse MobileNetV1 FPGA Accelerator With Chained Depthwise Separable Convolution and Computation-Aware Pruning
item.description: MobileNet has been widely adopted in mobile applications due to its lightweight architecture based on depthwise separable convolution (DSC). However, developing an efficient MobileNet accelerator remains hard as the DSC consists of two heterogeneous operations, depthwise convolution (DWC) and pointwise convolution (PWC). In addition, workload ratios between the DWC and PWC vary across the DSC layers, causing workload imbalance and thus underutilization in the accelerator. Pruning that removes unimportant weights worsens this problem as sparsity is not evenly distributed. In this brief, we propose an energy-efficient FPGA-based accelerator for sparse MobileNet with a novel operation called chained depthwise separable convolution (CDSC) and computation-aware pruning (CAP). The CDSC reformulates the consecutive DWC and PWC operations as a single operation, which resolves the underutilization problem by making a fixed workload ratio between the DWC and PWC in all DSC layers. Furthermore, the CDSC combines sparsities of the DWC and PWC, and this chained sparsity significantly reduces the computations of the CDSC-based MobileNet. To maximize the effect of the chained sparsity without significant accuracy loss, the CAP iteratively searches for efficient pruning targets by simultaneously considering the accuracy and the number of computations. The proposed accelerator is implemented on the Xilinx ZCU104 FPGA platform, and achieves the best trade-off between the accuracy and energy efficiency.

item.title: A 93.7% Peak Efficiency Compact Reconfigurable Switched-Capacitor DC–DC Converter With Soft VCR Transition
item.description: This brief proposes a compact reconfigurable switched-capacitor (SC) DC-DC converter targeting the miniaturization trend of Internet of Things (IoT) devices and dynamic voltage scaling (DVS) applications. The proposed topology utilizes only 21 switches and three flying capacitors (CFLY) to achieve step-down voltage conversion ratios (VCR) of 5:4/3/2/1, converting a 1.5 V input to a 0.16–1.19 V output. A soft VCR transition technique is employed to eliminate the hard-charging loss of the $C_{\mathrm {FLY}}$ , while an all-NMOS switch implementation is adopted to minimize switching losses. Fabricated in a 180 nm CMOS process, the converter achieves a measured steady-state peak power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 93.7%, supporting a maximum output current of 240 mA. Under periodic VCR transitions at 100 kHz, an average conversion efficiency as high as 85% is attained.

item.title: Distributed Data-Driven Dynamic Event-Triggered Control of Power Buffers in DC Microgrids
item.description: Direct current (DC) microgrids have attracted increasing attention due to their high efficiency and compatibility with renewable sources and energy storage systems. However, existing cooperative and communication-efficient control schemes for power buffers still rely heavily on accurate system models, which may limit performance under parameter variations and topology changes. This brief develops a distributed data-driven dynamic event-triggered control framework for power buffers in DC microgrids. Historical state-input trajectories are used to characterize the interconnected system and synthesize the controller directly, thereby avoiding explicit model identification. A dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM) is introduced to reduce unnecessary transmissions, and a model-free co-design of structured feedback gains and triggering weights is established via Lyapunov theory, the S-procedure, and linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). The design is centralized offline but distributed online: stacked trajectories are used only for LMI synthesis, while the implemented law follows the prescribed communication sparsity. Simulation results show that the proposed method achieves fast energy and voltage regulation under load disturbances while reducing communication burden compared with model-based and periodic communication strategies. Additional robustness discussions are included for representative parameter-perturbation and topology-change cases.

item.title: Fully Automated Schematic and Layout Design of Millimeter-Wave CMOS Power Amplifiers Using Prior Knowledge-Guided Decomposition and Machine Learning-Assisted Optimization
item.description: The RF CMOS technology is preferably used in the development of mass-market millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated circuits (ICs) because of its cost-effectiveness and integration capabilities. However, conventional design methods, limited by fixed topologies, struggle to achieve optimal performance, power, and area (PPA) tradeoffs. A fully automated method is proposed for rapid mmWave CMOS power amplifier (PA) design that uses prior knowledge-guided decomposition and machine learning-assisted optimization (MLAO). Following a hybrid topology configuration through schematic simulation, the proposed approach decomposes the entire circuit into multiple optimizable subproblems using microwave network theory. Then, these subproblems are solved sequentially and iteratively. In particular, a multibranch MLAO (MB-MLAO) algorithm is applied to on-chip transformers to enable broadband matching and high-fidelity impedance synthesis. Postlayout simulation results for five different PA design cases, spanning 17–41 GHz, demonstrate that the proposed method significantly accelerates the design process compared to conventional approaches while maintaining a high PPA.

item.title: Juggler: A Dynamic Warp Scheduler for GPGPUs
item.description: General-purpose graphics processing units (GPGPUs) accelerate various applications, ranging from graphics rendering to scientific simulations and machine learning (ML). The warp scheduler is a critical element in GPGPUs. It needs to manage thread execution in a way that optimizes performance as well as efficiency. However, different applications, and even different phases of the same application, have varying performance requirements. Hence, fixed static scheduling algorithms are suboptimal. This brief introduces a dynamic warp scheduler named Juggler, which dynamically switches between different scheduling strategies at runtime based on phase-specific performance characteristics. Juggler predicts and switches to the most suitable scheduling mode at runtime while improving the overall performance. Evaluations demonstrate that Juggler improves performance by up to 24.84%, with an average gain of 4.66% over state-of-the-art schedulers. These results emphasize the capability of dynamic scheduling to unlock even greater computational power of the GPGPUs.

item.title: Calibration and Enhancement of Analytical IR-Drop Model for Resistive Crossbar Arrays
item.description: Resistive in-memory computing (IMC) architectures emerged as a promising solution for efficiently accelerating neural network (NN) workloads on-chip, particularly in edge artificial intelligence (AI) applications where energy and area constraints are critical. Among the various challenges limiting IMC adoption, voltage drops caused by parasitic resistances significantly degrade the computational accuracy. While high-fidelity nodal analyses can model these effects accurately, their computational cost makes them unsuitable for system-level AI accelerator design. Analytical models offer a compelling alternative thanks to their speed and simplicity. However, the absence of a systematic method to fit them to different resistive memory devices and crossbar configurations might limit their applicability. In this work, we overcome this limitation by introducing a calibration procedure across a variety of input patterns and weight matrices. Furthermore, we evaluate the models under nonlinear $I$ – $V$ characteristics of resistive random access memory (RRAM) devices fabricated at IHP Microelectronics. Finally, we propose an enhanced analytical model for the better estimation of the voltage drops across the memory cells. Our modeling strategy is benchmarked against state-of-the-art approaches, achieving best-in-class performance among the analytical models in terms of accuracy and runtime. With more than two orders of magnitude improvement in simulation speed and a 5.9% median misalignment in the output currents approximation compared to SPICE-based nodal analysis, the presented solution is a compelling approach for evaluating large-scale IMC systems.

item.title: SwarmRouter: Obstacle-Avoiding Routing for Droplet Swarms on Active-Matrix Digital Microfluidic Biochips
item.description: Digital microfluidic biochips (DMFBs), renowned for their programmable and digital manipulations of droplets, have been extensively applied in the automation of bioassays. However, constrained by factors such as electrode size, quantity, and addressing methods, conventional DMFBs face challenges in deploying large-scale biochemical applications. In contrast, the next-generation active-matrix DMFs (AM-DMFs), leveraging their powerful capabilities in cross-addressing and parallel droplet manipulations, have emerged as a key alternative platform for high-throughput bioassays. Nevertheless, the execution of large-scale bioassays on the AM-DMF platforms poses significant challenges for droplet routing. For example, in single-cell (SC) proteomics assays, to facilitate high-throughput processing of numerous samples, hundreds and thousands of split droplets need to be transported in parallel to designated areas while avoiding on-chip obstacles. This gives rise to the large-scale obstacle-avoiding routing problem, which existing approaches prove inadequate to effectively address. In this article, we propose the first obstacle-avoiding routing method called SwarmRouter for large-scale droplet swarms, which enables efficient path planning for droplets while ensuring conflict-free and deadlock-free operations. The proposed method includes the following key techniques: 1) a geometric-temporal coupled preprocessing strategy integrating droplet spacing optimization and priority scheduling for conflict and deadlock elimination; 2) a path preselection strategy for both path length reduction and conflict avoidance; and 3) a timing-driven parallel routing method with dynamic checkpoints for waiting time minimization. Experimental results on an ACXEL AM16K biochip system demonstrate that SwarmRouter successfully realizes conflict-free path planning for all given droplets, while achieving significant reductions of 25.13% in total path length, 19.6% in maximum arrival time, and an improvement of 12.63% in average droplet velocity compared to a baseline method.

item.title: A High-Accuracy, Hybrid Scalable Model for MIM Capacitors Over Wide Temperature for MMIC Applications
item.description: Conventional process design kits (PDKs) for monolithic microwave integrated circuits (MMICs) often lack capacitor models that are robust across wide temperature and frequency ranges, posing a significant challenge to design reliability and first-pass success. To address this, a novel $\pi $ -type equivalent circuit with grounding inductors is developed, yielding S-parameter fitting errors under 2% while also explaining the device’s thermal resonant drift. Building on this, a hybrid scalable model synergizing a physics-guided core with neural network (NN) compensation is proposed. This methodology demonstrates exceptional accuracy, achieving parameter-fitting R-squared values above 0.999. More importantly, the final model’s S-parameter predictions maintain an R-squared greater than 0.98 against measured data across the entire temperature and geometry space. This work provides a highly accurate, scalable MIM capacitor model essential for robust circuit design under harsh operating conditions and offers a generalizable hybrid methodology applicable to other passive components, enhancing the predictive power of modern PDKs.

item.title: Unbalanced Ternary Full Adder Architecture in CNTFET Technology: Design and Application
item.description: Full adders are the fundamental building blocks of arithmetic units, directly influencing system performance and efficiency. Transitioning from binary to ternary computation offers substantial improvements in energy efficiency. This article proposes a novel ternary full adder (TFA) architecture implemented with 42 transistors using multithreshold carbon-nanotube field-effect transistor (CNTFET) technology. Circuit-level simulations performed in Synopsys HSPICE at 0.9 V demonstrate that the proposed TFA achieves a reduction of 35.8%–75.2% in power consumption and 21.6%–70% in energy consumption compared to state-of-the-art designs. Reliability analysis, based on extensive Monte Carlo (MC) simulations, confirms that the proposed architecture exhibits the lowest sensitivity to variations in key CNTFET process parameters. These advantages come at the expense of a moderate delay overhead and a $1.85\times $ increase in layout area relative to a highly compact design. To further validate its practical impact, the TFA is evaluated in an image-processing application leveraging ternary logic based on a hardware algorithm. The results indicate up to 38.86% energy savings while preserving accuracy and output quality. In addition, a comprehensive benchmarking framework is introduced, combining hardware efficiency and quality metrics into a unified figure of merit (FoM). Under this FoM, the proposed design outperforms the best existing counterpart by approximately 76.21%. The demonstrated tradeoff between energy efficiency and accuracy highlights the proposed CNTFET-based TFA as a promising candidate for the design of future high-performance and energy-aware ternary computing systems.

item.title: A Reduction-Based Fast Algorithm for Modeling Memristive Crossbar Array With IR-Drop Effect
item.description: The in-memory computing (IMC) based on memristive crossbar array (MCA) has attracted great attention due to its great potential to enable fast and energy-efficient matrix–vector multiplication (MVM). However, the IR-drop effect caused by wire resistance largely compromises the computational accuracy. Efficient modeling of IR-drop effect in large-scale MCAs is of great significance for their practical application. In this article, a highly efficient approach for accurately modeling the memristive array with IR-drop effect is proposed, which computes an equivalent conductance matrix to capture the relationship between the array’s input and output. It is based on a novel recursive network reduction approach that exploits the special topological structure of memristive array. For an $m~\times ~n$ array, the proposed approach has $O(\max (m,n)^{3})$ time complexity and $O(\max (m,n)^{2})$ space complexity, thus achieving a significant advantage over existing approaches. Numerical experiments with the memristive arrays on various sizes and wire resistances have validated the efficiency of the proposed approach. It is shown that the proposed approach runs over $55\times $ faster than the existing approach based on an advanced sparse direct solver on a $2048~\times ~2048$ array, without loss of accuracy.

item.title: ML-Based Abstract Power Modeling for Embedded System Processors
item.description: System-level power analysis is a critical requirement in modern embedded systems and mobile devices. This work focuses on enabling detailed power estimation for embedded processor cores within a core-based system-level design environment. Traditional register-transfer level (RTL) or gate-level simulation, while accurate, is too slow to support early system level decision making.
